positive_feedback: coopmat_store_col mirror discipline is exact: emit_coopmat_store_col_inline (crates/axc-codegen/src/coopmat.rs) is a byte-for-byte structural copy of emit_coopmat_store_inline — same access-chain construction, same call shape — with only the layout OpConstant flipped 0->1 (ROW_MAJOR_LAYOUT vs the new COL_MAJOR_LAYOUT). HIR (CoopMatBuiltin::StoreCol / CoopMatStoreLayout), typecheck (check_coopmat_store_stmt threaded with a layout param, ColMajor-targeting-shared correctly rejected), and body.rs dispatch (fail-closed defensive error if ColMajor ever reaches the Shared path, which typecheck already forbids) all follow the same side-by-side pattern the spec §3.1 mandated. Bonus: crates/axc-parser/src/parser.rs needed ZERO changes because its coopmat dispatch is already data-driven off axc_lexer::is_reserved_coopmat_builtin / RESERVED_COOPMAT_BUILTIN_NAMES (token.rs), which was updated — the spec's ~4 LOC parser estimate simply wasn't needed; not a deviation of concern, a favorable one.

The _ggml kernel (examples/q4km_matmul_rb_coopmat_f32acc_cached_ggml.axc) vs the M3.6 leader diffs to EXACTLY the six spec-enumerated deltas: (a) n_blocks_per_row derived from stride_a/256u32, (b) signature retyped to the 6 leading ggml push fields, (c-B) B retyped f32 + transposed index + f32_to_f16 staging convert, (c-D) D store swapped to coopmat_store_col with col*stride_d+row offsets, (e) block_row/block_col swapped onto gid(0)/gid(1). Every other executable line (the K-loop structure, the scale-cache fill/read, the barrier placement, the A-side dequant chain, the 2x2 coopmat mul_add geometry) is untouched. The doc-comment header was condensed/restructured rather than literally 'preserved verbatim with a prepended delta block', but it still covers BARRIERS/SHARED BOUNDS/NUMERICS/CAPABILITIES faithfully and is more honestly self-contained for a reader of just this file -- a documentation-only, disclosure-improving deviation, not a code-discipline violation.

upstream/REPRODUCE.md is genuinely usable by a llama.cpp maintainer unfamiliar with AXIOM: pinned SHA + tag, exact axc compile command with strategy values, exact byte-array embedding target (matmul_q4_k_f32_cm1_data[], explicitly distinguished from the wrong scalar/cm2 symbols), git apply --check/apply commands, and a clearly labeled 'KNOWN LIMITATION' section disclosing the one not-yet-compiled guard condition (#8's inline ggml_vk_guess_split_k call) instead of hiding it.

upstream/ggml-vulkan-axiom-q4k.patch is readable and the guard is fully commented: each of the 13 conditions carries an inline '// #N' tag matching the spec's §2.9 table, the header explains the three-hunk/two-site structure, and it correctly states the ONE known compile-fidelity caveat up front rather than presenting the patch as compile-verified when it isn't.

UPSTREAM_PR_PLAN.md diff: the status line and 'THE TRIGGER' paragraph are byte-identical pre/post (independently confirmed by re-reading both the pre-image via git diff context and the post-image text); all changes are additive (the M4.2a pointer, the rewritten items 2-4 referencing real artifacts, the appended two-checkbox RFC-open trigger-preconditions section). This matches the coder's claim and QA's independent byte-compare.

DESIGN.md §3.1.46 is accurate against the actual diff: the six deltas, the coopmat_store_col mechanism, the GPU-measured numbers (bit-identity, combined <=1e-3 incl. the rectangular shape), and the honest 0.505x/0.74-0.88x perf-sanity framing all match what the kernel/tests/upstream package actually contain.

AT-2810 (m313_tightlive_proxy_and_feasibility.rs) update from 4->5 builtins is minimal and correctly reasoned: it adds coopmat_store_col to the expected/reserved sets and explicitly re-states WHY the PRONG B BLOCKED verdict is unaffected (StoreCol is a whole-matrix store differing only in a layout operand, not a per-element fragment-write op) — the negative result's integrity is preserved, not just asserted.

The .gitignore fix (!upstream/*.spv placed after *.spv) and Cargo.toml bench registration are both clean, minimally scoped, and carry explanatory comments tying back to the AT/HIGH-finding they resolve.

AT-2998's hunk-anchoring check (m42a_patch_applies.rs) does real work: it parses '@@ -start,count' headers out of the patch text and checks them against the documented [4090,4211] / 8200..=8242 windows, rather than a superficial string search — it would actually catch a patch drifting to the :4429 fp16 tier as the r3 changelog claims.

minor_issues.description: Table row states leader TFLOPS at the A/B shape as 44.11, while DESIGN.md §3.1.46 prose and the coder's headline both cite 44.06 (ratio 0.505x consistent throughout). REPRODUCE.md's own text one paragraph below explains criterion vs one-shot measurements 'may differ slightly run-to-run', so this is disclosed run-to-run variance rather than a hidden contradiction, but a single canonical number (or explicitly labeling which is one-shot vs criterion in the table) would remove the need for a reader to infer that from prose.

The M3.6 mechanism/barriers/numerics header comment was condensed rather than kept verbatim-plus-prepended as the spec §4 preamble literally states. Content-complete and arguably clearer standalone, but technically a wording deviation from the spec's stated discipline for the comment block (the CODE is unaffected).

summary: Implementation matches the r3-agreed spec closely. The coopmat_store_col builtin is a faithful side-by-side mirror of coopmat_store at every lowering stage (HIR/typecheck/codegen), including a correct typecheck-time rejection of shared-array targets and a defensive fail-closed codegen error backing that invariant. The _ggml kernel diffs cleanly to exactly the six enumerated ABI deltas with no unlisted changes to the K-loop, barriers, or dequant chain. The upstream/ package (patch, byte-array fragment, REPRODUCE.md) is genuinely usable and honestly discloses its one open compile-fidelity caveat rather than overclaiming. UPSTREAM_PR_PLAN.md's HOLD status and trigger paragraph are provably untouched; DESIGN.md §3.1.46 accurately reflects the shipped artifacts and measured numbers; the AT-2810 4->5 builtin update correctly preserves the M3.13 PRONG B BLOCKED verdict's reasoning. LOC breakdown (per QA's independent recount, ~3192-3226 vs the coder's claimed 3186) is honest and not padded. Only two cosmetic/documentation-level nits found, neither affecting correctness, scope, or spec compliance.
